approachQuestion.prompt:
For every integer from zero through N inclusive, count its set bits in a W-bit representation. Return the sum of all those counts. The integers are specified by N, not supplied as an array.

Constraints: 1 <= W <= 32; 0 <= N < 2^W. Return an exact unsigned 64-bit total.
Example: W=3, N=5 -> 7, because counts for 0..5 are 0,1,1,2,1,2. Edge case: N=0 -> 0.

Choose the best approach under these constraints.
constraints: W is a width parameter. Unsigned 64-bit arithmetic, division, shifts and comparisons have constant cost. All intermediates, including N+1, 2^(b+1), and the final sum, fit in 64 bits.
Inputs are read-only. Include all temporary storage and any call stack; exclude the supplied input and the returned output. No input copy is implicit.

options.text: For each position b=0..W-1, let h=2^b and t=N+1. Add floor(t/(2h))*h + max(0,(t mod 2h)-h) to the total.
options.feedback: At position b, blocks of h zero bits alternate with blocks of h one bits. Complete periods and the final partial period account for all t integers exactly.

options.text: Enumerate every value from zero through N and count its set bits, accumulating the counts.
options.feedback: The exact total is found, but enumeration may visit far more values than there are bit positions.

options.text: Return (N+1) times the popcount of N.
options.feedback: Earlier integers need not have the same number of ones. For N=2 this gives 3 instead of the correct total 2.

options.text: Use the same per-position periods, but add only floor((N+1)/(2h))*h and ignore the final partial period.
options.feedback: Partial periods may contain ones. For N=2, position 1 contributes one from the partial block; omitting it gives 1 instead of total 2.

feedback.reason: For each bit position, zero/one runs repeat in periods.
details: At each bit position, count complete zero/one periods across the N+1 integers and then count any ones in the remaining partial period. Add each position contribution to a 64-bit total without generating the integers.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For count-periodic-bit-blocks, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let W be the representation width.
constraints: W is a width parameter. Unsigned 64-bit arithmetic, division, shifts and comparisons have constant cost. All intermediates, including N+1, 2^(b+1), and the final sum, fit in 64 bits.

feedback.reason: One arithmetic contribution per bit position is independent of the number of integers.
details: The specified loop performs fixed arithmetic at each of W positions, regardless of N. A position counter and a few 64-bit quantities suffice; there is no recursion or generated interval array.

“O(N+1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: This describes enumerating all values with constant-time popcount.
“O(W) time, O(W) auxiliary space”: The loop retains only a few scalars, not a table per position.
“O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The specified method iterates across W positions; W is a parameter.
